chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man has an oath upon him, so his creditor makes him swear with the harsh oath that he cannot leave the city except by letting him know.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He should not go out until he lets him know.' I said, 'If he lets him know, he will not let him go.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If his letting him know is harmful to him and to his family, then let him go out, and there is nothing upon him (no expiation).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a debtor's oath to notify his creditor causes him harm?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia legal principle of 'al-darar yuzal' (harm is removed), where the creditor's right to notification yields to the debtor's need to avoid significant detriment. It highlights the juristic balance between enforcing contractual oaths and preventing undue hardship, allowing the debtor to depart if the act of informing the creditor would cause tangible harm to him or his dependents.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Sahl, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man happens to have an oath upon him, so his creditor gets him to swear with the harsh oath that he cannot leave from the city except by letting him know’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not go out until he lets him know’ I said, ‘If he lets him know, he would not leave him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his letting him know is harmful upon him and upon his family, so let him go out, and there is nothing upon him (expiation)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sahl from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is under oath and his creditor makes him to take an oath with all seriousness not to leave the town without his knowledge. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must not leave the town without his knowledge.’ I then said that if he informs, he would not allow him to go out. He (the Imam) said, ‘If informing him is harmful to him and his family he can go out and he does not owe anything.’”
